text:
Let $A=\{z\in C:1\leq |z-(1+i)|\leq 2\}$

and $B=\{z\in A:|z-(1-i)|=1\}$. Then, B :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $z=x+iy$

Given, $1\leq |z-(1+i)|\leq 2$

$\Rightarrow 1\leq |x+iy-1-i|\leq 2$

$\Rightarrow 1\leq |(x-1)+i(y-1)|\leq 2$

$\Rightarrow 1\leq \sqrt{(x-1)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}}\leq 2$

It represents two concentric circles both have center at (1, 1) and radius 1 and 2.


[IMG]


Also given,

$|z-(1-i)|=1$

$\Rightarrow |x+iy-1+i|=1$

$\Rightarrow |(x-1)+i(y+1)|=1$

$\Rightarrow \sqrt{(x-1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2}}=1$

This represents a circle with center at (1, $-$1) and radius = 1.


[IMG]


In the common region infinite values of B possible.

text: The surface area of a balloon of spherical shape being inflated, increases at a constant rate. If initially, the radius of balloon is 3 units and after 5 seconds, it becomes 7 units, then its radius after 9 seconds is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The surface area is $S=4πr^{2}$ and $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=k$ (constant), so $S$ is linear in time:

$S=S_{0}+kt$

At $t=0$, $r=3$, so $S_{0}=36π$. At $t=5$, $r=7$, so $S=196π$:

$36π+5k=196π\Rightarrow k=32π$

At $t=9$:

$4πr^{2}=36π+32π(9)=324π\Rightarrow r^{2}=81\Rightarrow r=9$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text: Bag A contains 2 white, 1 black and 3 red balls and bag B contains 3 black, 2 red and n white balls. One bag is chosen at random and 2 balls drawn from it at random, are found to be 1 red and 1 black. If the probability that both balls come from Bag A is $\frac{6}{11}$, then n is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

$\begin{array}{l} P(1R\text{and}1B)=P(A)\cdot P\left (\dfrac{1R1B}{A}\right )+P(B)\cdot P\left (\dfrac{1R1B}{B}\right ) \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \dfrac{{}^{3}C_{1}\cdot {}^{1}C_{1}}{{}^{6}C_{2}}+\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \dfrac{{}^{2}C_{1}\cdot {}^{3}C_{1}}{{}^{n+5}C_{2}} \\  \\ P\left (\dfrac{1R1B}{A}\right )=\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{15}}{\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{15}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{6\cdot 2}{(n+5)(n+4)}}=\dfrac{6}{11} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\frac{1}{10}}{\frac{1}{10}+\frac{6}{(n+5)(n+4)}}=\dfrac{6}{11} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \dfrac{11}{10}=\dfrac{6}{10}+\dfrac{36}{(n+5)(n+4)} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{5}{10\times 36}=\dfrac{1}{(n+5)(n+4)} \\  \\ \Rightarrow n^{2}+9n-52=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow n=4\text{is only possible value} \end{array}$

x + y + z = $α$

is inconsistent, is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

Now check for $α=1$

text:
If the sum of the squares of the reciprocals of the roots $α$ and $β$ of 

the equation $3x^{2} +$ $λ$x $-$ 1 = 0 is 15, then 6($α^{3}$ + $β^{3})^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$3x^{2}+λx-1=0$

Given, two roots are $α$ and $β$.

$\therefore$ Sum of roots $=α+β=\frac{-λ}{3}$

And product of roots $=αβ=\frac{-1}{3}$

Given that,

Sum of square of reciprocal of roots $α$ and $β$ is 15.

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{α^{2}}+\frac{1}{β^{2}}=15$

$\Rightarrow \frac{α^{2}+β^{2}}{α^{2}β^{2}}=15$

$\Rightarrow \frac{(α+β)^{2}-2αβ}{(αβ)^{2}}=15$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\frac{λ2}{9}+2\times \frac{1}{3}}{\frac{1}{9}}=15$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\frac{λ2+6}{9}}{\frac{1}{9}}=15$

$\Rightarrow λ^{2}+6=15$

$\Rightarrow λ^{2}=9$

Now, $6(α^{3}+β^{3})^{2}$

$=6\{(α+β)(α^{2}+β^{2}-αβ)\}^{2}$

$=6(α+β)^{2}\left [(α+β)^{2}-2αβ-αβ\right ]^{2}$

$=6\left (\frac{-λ}{3}\right )^{2}\left [\left (\frac{-λ}{3}\right )^{2}-3.\frac{-1}{3}\right ]^{2}$

$=6\times \frac{λ^{2}}{9}\times \left [\frac{λ^{2}}{9}+1\right ]^{2}$

$=6\times \frac{9}{9}\times \left [\frac{9}{9}+1\right ]^{2}$

$=6\times (2)^{2}$

$=6\times 4=24$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text:
The set of all values of k for which 

$(\tan ^{-1}x)^{3}+(\cot ^{-1}x)^{3}=kπ^{3},x\in R$, is the interval :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(\tan ^{-1}x)^{3}+(\cot ^{-1}x)^{3}=kπ^{3}$

Let $f(t)=t^{3}+\left (\frac{π}{2}-t\right )^{3}$

Where $t=\tan ^{-1}x$ ; $t\in \left (-\frac{π}{2},\frac{π}{2}\right )$

$=t^{3}+\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )^{3}-\frac{3π^{2}t}{4}+\frac{3π}{2}t^{2}-t^{3}$

$f(t)=\frac{3π}{2}t^{2}-\frac{3π^{2}}{4}.t+\frac{π^{3}}{8}$

This is a quadratic equation of t.

Here, coefficient of $t^{2}$ term is $\frac{3π}{2}$ which is > 0.

$\therefore$ It is an upward parabola.

Now, $f^{'}(t)=3πt-\frac{3π^{2}}{4}$

$f^{''}(t)=3π>0$

$\therefore$ $3πt-\frac{3π^{2}}{4}=0$

$\Rightarrow t=\frac{π}{4}$ (minima)

$\therefore$ vertex of graph at $\frac{π}{4}$

 
[IMG]
 

$\therefore$ Minimum value at $\frac{π}{4}$ and maximum value at $-\frac{π}{2}$.

$\therefore$ $f\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=\frac{π^{3}}{64}+\left (\frac{π}{2}-\frac{π}{4}\right )^{3}=\frac{π^{3}}{32}$

$f\left (-\frac{π}{2}\right )=-\frac{π^{3}}{8}+π^{3}$

$=\frac{7π^{3}}{8}$

$\therefore$ $kπ^{3}\in \left [\frac{π^{3}}{32},\frac{7π^{3}}{8}\right )$

$\Rightarrow k\in \left [\frac{1}{32},\frac{7}{8}\right )$

text: The sum of absolute maximum and absolute minimum values of the function $f(x)=|2x^{2}+3x-2|+\sin x\cos x$ in the interval [0, 1] is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=|(2x-1)(x+2)|+\frac{\sin 2x}{2}$

$0\leq x<\frac{1}{2}f(x)=(1-2x)(x+2)+\frac{\sin 2x}{2}$

$f^{'}(x)=-4x-3+\cos 2x<0$

For $x\geq \frac{1}{2}:f^{'}(x)=4x+3+\cos 2x>0$

So, minima occurs at $x=\frac{1}{2}$

$\begin{array}{ll} f(x)|_{\min } & =\left |2\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )^{2}+\dfrac{3}{2}-2\right |+\sin \left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )\cdot \cos \left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right ) \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 1 \end{array}$

So, maxima is possible at $x=0$ or $x=1$

Now checking for $x=0$ and $x=1$, we can see it attains its maximum value at $x=1$

$\begin{array}{ll} f(x)|_{\max }= & |2+3-2|+\dfrac{\sin 2}{2} \\  \\ =3+\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2 \end{array}$

Sum of absolute maximum and minimum value 

$=3+\frac{1}{2}(\sin 1+\sin 2)$

$=3+\frac{1}{2}(\sin 1+2\sin 1\cos 1)$

= $3+\frac{1}{2}(1+2\cos (1))\sin (1)$

text: If $\{a_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}$, where n is an even integer, is an arithmetic progression with common difference 1, and $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}a_{i}=192,\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n/2}a_{2i}=120$, then n is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}a_{i}=192$

$\Rightarrow$ $a_{1} + a_{2} + a_{3} + ...... + a_{n} = 192$

$\Rightarrow \frac{n}{2}[a_{1}+a_{n}]=192$

$\Rightarrow a_{1}+a_{n}=\frac{384}{n}$ ..... (1)

Now, $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{\frac{n}{2}}a_{2i}=120$

$\Rightarrow$ $a_{2} + a_{4} + a_{6} + ...... + a_{n} = 120$

Here total $\frac{n}{2}$ terms present.

$\therefore$ $\frac{\frac{n}{2}}{2}[a_{2}+a_{n}]=120$

$\Rightarrow \frac{n}{4}[a_{1}+1+a_{n}]=120$

$\Rightarrow a_{1}+a_{n}+1=\frac{480}{n}$ ..... (2)

Subtracting (1) from (2), we get

$1=\frac{480}{n}-\frac{384}{n}$

$\Rightarrow 1=\frac{96}{n}$

$\Rightarrow$ n = 96
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text:
If x = x(y) is the solution of the differential equation 

$y\frac{dx}{dy}=2x+y^{3}(y+1)e^{y},x(1)=0$; then x(e) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dx}{dy}-\frac{2x}{y}=y^{2}(y+1)e^{y}$

$\text{I.F.}=e^{\int -\frac{2}{y}dy}=e^{-2\ln y}=\frac{1}{y^{2}}$

Solution is given by

$\begin{array}{ll} \quad x\cdot \dfrac{1}{y^{2}}=\int y^{2}(y+1)e^{y}\cdot \dfrac{1}{y^{2}}dy \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & \dfrac{x}{y^{2}}=\int (y+1)e^{y}dy \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & \dfrac{x}{y^{2}}=ye^{y}+c \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow x=y^{2}(ye^{y}+c)$ at, $y=1,x=0$

$\Rightarrow 0=1\left (1\cdot e^{1}+c\right )\Rightarrow c=-e$ at $y=e$,

$x=e^{2}(e.e^{e}-e)$

text: Let $\widehat{a}$, $\hat{b}$ be unit vectors. If $\vec{c}$ be a vector such that the angle between $\widehat{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $\frac{π}{12}$, and $\hat{b}=\vec{c}+2\left (\vec{c}\times \widehat{a}\right )$, then $\left |6\vec{c}\right |^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because \hat{b}=⃗{c}+2(⃗{c}\times \hat{a})$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \hat{b}\cdot ⃗{c}=|⃗{c}|^{2} \\  \\ \therefore \hat{b}-⃗{c}=2(⃗{c}\times ⃗{a}) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow |\hat{b}|^{2}+|⃗{c}|^{2}-2\hat{b}\cdot ⃗{c}=4|⃗{c}|^{2}|⃗{a}|^{2}\sin ^{2}\dfrac{π}{12} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 1+|⃗{c}|^{2}-2|c|^{2}=4|⃗{c}|^{2}\left (\dfrac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2\sqrt{2}}\right )^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 1=|⃗{c}|^{2}(3-\sqrt{3}) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 36|⃗{c}|^{2}=\dfrac{36}{3-\sqrt{3}}=6(3+\sqrt{3}) \end{array}$

text:
The domain of the function 

$f(x)=\frac{\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{x2-5x+6}{x2-9}\right )}{\log _{e}(x^{2}-3x+2)}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $x^{2}-5x+6=(x-2)(x-3)$ and $x^{2}-9=(x-3)(x+3)$, the argument of $\cos ^{-1}$ is defined only for $x\neq \pm 3$, where it equals $\dfrac{x-2}{x+3}$, and it must satisfy $-1\leq \dfrac{x-2}{x+3}\leq 1$.

$\dfrac{x-2}{x+3}\leq 1⇔\dfrac{-5}{x+3}\leq 0⇔x>-3$.

$\dfrac{x-2}{x+3}\geq -1⇔\dfrac{2x+1}{x+3}\geq 0⇔x<-3$ or $x\geq -\dfrac{1}{2}$.

So the numerator needs $x\in \left [-\dfrac{1}{2},\infty \right )-\{3\}$.

For the denominator, $x^{2}-3x+2=(x-1)(x-2)>0$ gives $x\in (-\infty ,1)\cup (2,\infty )$, and $\log _{e}(x^{2}-3x+2)\neq 0$ needs $x^{2}-3x+1\neq 0$, that is $x\neq \dfrac{3\pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$.

Here $\dfrac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\approx 0.38$ lies in $\left [-\dfrac{1}{2},1\right )$, while $\dfrac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}\approx 2.62$ and $3$ lie in $(2,\infty )$, so the domain is

$\left [-\frac{1}{2},1\right )\cup (2,\infty )-\left \{3,\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2},\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\right \}.$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text:
The number of one-one functions f : {a, b, c, d} $\to$ {0, 1, 2, ......, 10} such 

that 2f(a) $-$ f(b) + 3f(c) + f(d) = 0 is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given one-one function

$f:\{a,b,c,d\}\to \{0,1,2,....10\}$

and $2f(a)-f(b)+3f(c)+f(d)=0$

$\Rightarrow 3f(c)+2f(a)+f(d)=f(b)$

Case I:

(1) Now let $f(c)=0$ and $f(a)=1$ then

$3\times 0+2\times 1+f(d)=f(b)$

$\Rightarrow 2+f(d)=f(b)$

Now possible value of $f(d)=2,3,4,5,6,7,$ and $8$.

f(d) can't be 9 and 10 as if $f(d)=9$ or 10 then $f(b)=2+9=11$ or $f(b)=2+10=12$, which is not possible as here any function's maximum value can be 10.

$\therefore$ Total possible functions when $f(c)=0$ and $f(a)=1$ are = 7

(2) When $f(c)=0$ and $f(a)=2$ then

$3\times 0+2\times 2+f(d)=f(b)$

$\Rightarrow 4+f(d)=f(b)$

$\therefore$ possible value of $f(d)=1,3,4,5,6$

$\therefore$ Total possible functions in this case = 5

(3) When $f(c)=0$ and $f(a)=3$ then

$3\times 0+2\times 3+f(d)=f(b)$

$\Rightarrow 6+f(d)=f(b)$

$\therefore$ Possible value of $f(d)=1,2,4$

$\therefore$ Total possible functions in this case = 3

(4) When $f(c)=0$ and $f(a)=4$ then

$3\times 0+2\times 4+f(d)=f(b)$

$\Rightarrow 8+f(d)=f(b)$

$\therefore$ Possible value of $f(d)=1,2$

$\therefore$ Total possible functions in this case = 2

(5) When $f(c)=0$ and $f(a)=5$ then

$3\times 0+2\times 5+f(d)=f(b)$

$\Rightarrow 10+f(d)=f(b)$

Possible value of f(d) can be 0 but f(c) is already zero. So, no value to f(d) can satisfy.

$\therefore$ No function is possible in this case.

$\therefore$ Total possible functions when $f(c)=0$ and $f(a)=1,2,3$ and $4$ are $=7+5+3+2=17$

Case II:

(1) When $f(c)=1$ and $f(a)=0$ then

$3\times 1+2\times 0+f(d)=f(b)$

$\Rightarrow 3+f(d)=f(b)$

$\therefore$ Possible value of $f(d)=2,3,4,5,6,7$

$\therefore$ Total possible functions in this case = 6

(2) When $f(c)=1$ and $f(a)=2$ then

$3\times 1+2\times 2+f(d)=f(b)$

$\Rightarrow 7+f(d)=f(b)$

$\therefore$ Possible value of $f(d)=0,3$

$\therefore$ Total possible functions in this case = 2

(3) When $f(c)=1$ and $f(a)=3$ then

$3\times 1+2\times 3+f(d)=f(b)$

$\Rightarrow 9+f(d)=f(b)$

$\therefore$ Possible value of $f(d)=0$

$\therefore$ Total possible functions in this case = 1

$\therefore$ Total possible functions when $f(c)=1$ and $f(a)=0,2$ and $3$ are

$=6+2+1=9$

Case III:

(1) When $f(c)=2$ and $f(a)=0$ then

$3\times 2+2\times 0+f(d)=f(b)$

$\Rightarrow 6+f(d)=f(b)$

$\therefore$ Possible values of $f(d)=1,3,4$

$\therefore$ Total possible functions in this case = 3

(2) When $f(c)=2$ and $f(a)=1$ then,

$3\times 2+2\times 1+f(d)=f(b)$

$\Rightarrow 8+f(d)=f(b)$

$\therefore$ Possible values of $f(d)=0$

$\therefore$ Total possible function in this case = 1

$\therefore$ Total possible functions when $f(c)=2$ and $f(a)=0,1$ are

$=3+1=4$

Case IV:

(1) When $f(c)=3$ and $f(a)=0$ then

$3\times 3+2\times 0+f(d)=f(b)$

$\Rightarrow 9+f(d)=f(b)$

$\therefore$ Possible values of $f(d)=1$

$\therefore$ Total one-one functions from four cases

$=17+9+4+1=31$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text: In an examination, there are 5 multiple choice questions with 3 choices, out of which exactly one is correct. There are 3 marks for each correct answer, $-$2 marks for each wrong answer and 0 mark if the question is not attempted. Then, the number of ways a student appearing in the examination gets 5 marks is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let student marks $x$ correct answers and $y$ incorrect. So

$3x-2y=5$ and $x+y\leq 5$ where $x,y\in \mathrm{W}$

Only possible solution is $(x,y)=(3,2)$

Students can mark correct answers by only one choice but for an incorrect answer, there are two choices. So total number of ways of scoring 5 marks $={}^{5}C_{3}(1)^{3}\cdot (2)^{2}=40$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text: Let $A\left (\frac{3}{\sqrt{a}},\sqrt{a}\right ),a>0$, be a fixed point in the xy-plane. The image of A in y-axis be B and the image of B in x-axis be C. If $D(3\cos θ,a\sin θ)$ is a point in the fourth quadrant such that the maximum area of $\Delta$ACD is 12 square units, then a is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
$B=\left (-\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}},\sqrt{a}\right )$ and $C=\left (-\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}},-\sqrt{a}\right )$, so $C$ is the reflection of $A$ in the origin.

Area of $△ACD$ is $\Delta =\dfrac{1}{2}|M|$, where

$M=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}} & \sqrt{a} & 1 \\ -\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}} & -\sqrt{a} & 1 \\ 3\cos θ & a\sin θ & 1 \end{array}\right |$

Applying $R_{1}\to R_{1}+R_{2}$ makes the first row $(0,0,2)$, so

$M=2\left [-\frac{3}{\sqrt{a}}\cdot a\sin θ+\sqrt{a}\cdot 3\cos θ\right ]=6\sqrt{a}(\cos θ-\sin θ)$

So $\Delta =3\sqrt{a}|\cos θ-\sin θ|$.

For $D$ in the fourth quadrant, $θ\in \left (-\dfrac{π}{2},0\right )$, and $\cos θ-\sin θ=\sqrt{2}\cos \left (θ+\dfrac{π}{4}\right )$ has maximum $\sqrt{2}$, reached at $θ=-\dfrac{π}{4}$.

$\Delta _{\max }=3\sqrt{2a}=12\Rightarrow 2a=16\Rightarrow a=8$

Hence, the answer is 8.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text: Let a line having direction ratios, 1, $-$4, 2 intersect the lines $\frac{x-7}{3}=\frac{y-1}{-1}=\frac{z+2}{1}$ and $\frac{x}{2}=\frac{y-7}{3}=\frac{z}{1}$ at the points A and B. Then $(AB)^{2}$ is equal to $___________$.

solution.body:
Let $A(3λ+7,-λ+1,λ-2)$ and $B(2μ,3μ+7,μ)$ 

So, DR's of $AB\propto 3λ-2μ+7,-(λ+3μ+6),λ-μ$ $-2$

Clearly $\frac{3λ-2μ+7}{1}=\frac{λ+3μ+6}{4}=\frac{λ-μ-2}{2}$

$\Rightarrow 5λ-3μ=-16$

And $λ-5μ=10$

From (i) and (ii) we get $λ=-5,μ=-3$

So, $A$ is $(-8,6,-7)$ and $B$ is $(-6,-2,-3)$

$AB=\sqrt{4+64+16}\Rightarrow (AB)^{2}=84$

text:
The number of points where the function

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{lll} |2x^{2}-3x-7| & if & x\leq -1 \\ [4x^{2}-1] & if & -1<x<1 \\ |x+1|+|x-2| & if & x\geq 1 \end{array} \right.$

[t] denotes the greatest integer $\leq$ t, is discontinuous is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At $x=-1$: $f(-1)=|2+3-7|=2$, and as $x\to -1^{+}$, $4x^{2}-1\to 3^{-}$, so $[4x^{2}-1]\to 2$. Hence $f$ is continuous at $x=-1$.

At $x=1$: $f(1)=|2|+|-1|=3$, while as $x\to 1^{-}$, $[4x^{2}-1]\to 2$. Hence $f$ is discontinuous at $x=1$.

For $x\leq -1$ the function $|2x^{2}-3x-7|$ and for $x\geq 1$ the function $|x+1|+|x-2|$ are continuous.

For $-1<x<1$, $4x^{2}-1\in [-1,3)$. The value $-1$ occurs only at $x=0$, a minimum; near $x=0$, $4x^{2}-1\in [-1,0)$, so $[4x^{2}-1]=-1$ and $f$ is continuous at $x=0$.

$[4x^{2}-1]$ jumps wherever $4x^{2}-1$ crosses an integer:

$4x^{2}-1=0,1,2\Rightarrow x=\pm \dfrac{1}{2},\pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

These 6 points together with $x=1$ give 7 points of discontinuity.

Hence, the answer is 7.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text: Let $f(θ)=\sin θ+\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}(\sin θ+t\cos θ)f(t)dt$. Then the value of $\left |\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}f(θ)dθ\right |$ is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(θ)=\sin θ\left (1+\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}f(t)dt\right )+\cos θ\left (\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}tf(t)dt\right )$

Clearly $f(θ)=a\sin θ+b\cos θ$

Where $a=1+\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}(a\sin t+b\cos t)dt\Rightarrow a=1+2b...(i)$

and $b=\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}(at\sin t+bt\cos t)dt\Rightarrow b=2a...(ii)$

from (i) and (ii) we get

$a=-\frac{1}{3}\text{and}b=-\frac{2}{3}$

So $f(θ)=-\frac{1}{3}(\sin θ+2\cos θ)$

$\Rightarrow \left |\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}f(θ)dθ\right |=\frac{1}{3}(1+2\times 1)=1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text:
Let $Max_{0\leq x\leq 2}\left \{\frac{9-x^{2}}{5-x}\right \}=α$ and $Min_{0\leq x\leq 2}\left \{\frac{9-x^{2}}{5-x}\right \}=β$.

If $\int\limits _{β-\frac{8}{3}}^{2α-1}Max\left \{\frac{9-x^{2}}{5-x},x\right \}dx=α_{1}+α_{2}\log _{e}\left (\frac{8}{15}\right )$ then $α_{1}+α_{2}$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $f(x)=\frac{x^{2}-9}{x-5}\Rightarrow f^{'}(x)=\frac{(x-1)(x-9)}{(x-5)^{2}}$

So, $α=f(1)=2$ and $β=\min (f(0),f(2))=\frac{5}{3}$

Now, $\int\limits _{-1}^{3}\max \left \{\frac{x^{2}-9}{x-5},x\right \}dx=\int\limits _{-1}^{9/5}\frac{x^{2}-9}{x-5}dx+\int\limits _{9/5}^{3}xdx$

$=\int\limits _{-1}^{9/5}\left (x+5+\frac{16}{x-5}\right )dx+\frac{x^{2}}{2}\left |_{9/5}^{3} \right.$

$=\frac{28}{25}+14+16\ln \left (\frac{8}{15}\right )+\frac{72}{25}=18+16\ln \left (\frac{8}{15}\right )$

Clearly $α_{1}=18$ and $α_{2}=16$, so $α_{1}+α_{2}=34$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text: Let S be the region bounded by the curves $y = x^{3}$ and $y^{2} = x$. The curve y = 2|x| divides S into two regions of areas $R_{1}, R_{2}$. If $\max  {R_{1}, R_{2}} = R_{2}$, then $\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}}$ is equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

$C_{1}:y=x^{3}$

 $C_{2}:y^{2}=x$

and $C_{3}=y=2|x|$

$C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ intersect at $(1,1)$

$C_{2}$ and $C_{3}$ intersect at $\left (\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{2}\right )$

Clearly $R_{1}=\int\limits _{0}^{1/4}(\sqrt{x}-2x)dx=\frac{2}{3}\left (\frac{1}{8}\right )-\frac{1}{16}=\frac{1}{48}$

and $R_{1}+R_{2}=\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (\sqrt{x}-x^{3}\right )dx=\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{5}{12}$

So, $\frac{R_{1}+R_{2}}{R_{1}}=\frac{5/12}{1/48}\Rightarrow 1+\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}}=20$

$\Rightarrow \frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}}=19$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text:
If the shortest distance between the lines 

$\vec{r}=\left (-\hat{i}+3\widehat{k}\right )+λ\left (\hat{i}-a\hat{j}\right )$ 

and $\vec{r}=\left (-\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}\right )+μ\left (\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\widehat{k}\right )$ is $\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}$, then the integral value of a is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -a & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{array}\right |=-a\hat{i}-\hat{j}+(a-1)\hat{k}$ 

$⃗{a}_{1}-⃗{a}_{2}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$

Shortest distance $=\left |\frac{\left (⃗{a}_{1}-⃗{a}_{2}\right )\cdot \left (⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2}\right )}{\right |⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2}\left |}\right |$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}=\dfrac{2(a-1)}{\sqrt{a^{2}+1+(a-1)^{2}}} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 6\left (a^{2}-2a+1\right )=2a^{2}-2a+2 \\  \\ \Rightarrow (a-2)(2a-1)=0\Rightarrow a=2\text{because}a\in z. \end{array}$
